svg.text: Sensor views on the 3-D map — night vision and thermal, one shared post-process (CE-1984 / CE-1985)
Annotations in grey are not drawn by the app. Every panel is the SAME scene; only the light (night vision) or the time of day (thermal) changes.
A · NIGHT VISION — the scene lit by the REAL light (sun · moon · stars), the tube's gain brings it up, grain grows as the light falls
A1 · full moon (~0.2 lux)
clean picture, the trees bright (leaves reflect near-infrared)
A2 · starlight, overcast (~0.001 lux)
the same gain, far more grain (noise ∝ 1/√light)
A3 · a muzzle flash in view
the bright source blooms, the gain pulls everything else down
a lamp that is ON (VehicleLights, brake lights derived):
drawn bright and blooming — it lights nothing around it
a burning spot, a flame jet, a flash, a blast:
the effect layer's own list — bright, blooming
the automatic gain dims the scene while a
bright source is on screen (A3 vs A1)
B · THERMAL (white-hot) — the same scene through the day: surfaces by α (absorption) · τ (inertia) · ε (emissivity), units by their heat
B1 · noon, sunny
the road hottest; a parked tank sun-warm; low contrast on the man
B2 · dusk
the crossover: road and field close; the pond ≈ land
B3 · 3 am, clear
road, pond above the field; cold tank, roof, glass below
B4 · 3 am, overcast
flat: clouds stop the cooling; units stand out
a ground heat mark (TD-14): where a vehicle idled —
warm for its cooling time, never drawn in the normal view
the idling tank: hull at the metal surface temperature +
the engine's heat at its hot end (the AI's calculator, in °C)
glass and metal reflect the sky:
cold under a clear night sky
C · THE CONTROLS — View menu, the legend strip on the map, the hover readout

hover any unit in thermal: its temperature and WHY
(the drivers the AI's sensor reads); in night
vision: its light level and lamps
drawn after the post-process: sharp, never grainy or green
Scope: the two sensor views, their menu items, the legend strips and the hover readout. Everything else on the map (panels, HUD, the 2-D map,
the normal 3-D view) is unchanged except for row D. Lamps, flames, flashes and embers are SEEN in every view and light their surroundings (no shadows) except in thermal (R-1057).
⭐ The labels and cards a layer draws in screen space stay on top, sharp; the 3-D gizmos are part of the scene and take the sensor's look.
D · LIGHT SOURCES at night — headlamps, a blast, a muzzle flash, a burning cigarette: SEEN in every view, LIGHTING their surroundings (no shadows) except in thermal
D1 · NORMAL view, night
lamps / blast / flash light pools around them (cheap, no shadows)
D2 · NIGHT VISION
the same pools amplified; every source blooms; the ember is a bright point
D3 · THERMAL
no light pools (light is not heat); blast, flash and ember saturate, the lamp is warm
the cigarette's ember: brighter while it is at his lips (the drag, on the
smoker's own idle clock) — a 0.4 m light, seen in every view
the muzzle flash: a 6 m light for 60 ms, a
bloom in night vision, saturated in thermal
F4 cycles: normal → night vision → thermal → normal
(the legend strip names the view and "F4: next")
